hero.title: Brushland
hero.description: Brushland is a cozy fairytale kingdom-builder from Transhuman Design: you paint the land directly — mountains, rivers, waterfalls, roads — and the kingdom builds itself. Villagers move in automatically, and houses change appearance depending on their surroundings, so every painted hillside grows into a living storybook village. Revealed with an official trailer at The MIX Fall Game Showcase on October 16, 2026, and now wishlishtable on Steam, this wiki tracks Brushland from reveal to release: how the painting works, what the villagers and houses do, what the trailer shows, and when you can play it.

aboutGame.title: What Is Brushland?
paragraphs: Brushland is a kingdom-builder with the soul of a picture book, developed by Transhuman Design — the veteran indie studio whose developer Michał introduced the game on its new Steam page. The premise in one breath: you paint the land, and the kingdom builds itself. Mountains rise where you stroke a ridge, rivers run where you draw a valley, waterfalls pour off your painted cliffs — and villagers, unprompted, move in, settle, and raise houses that change appearance depending on what surrounds them. There are no grids and no placement menus; the terrain brush is the entire interface, and the fairytale kingdom is its consequence.

The game went viral on October 16, 2026, when the official gameplay trailer debuted at The MIX Fall Online Game Showcase and social channels like Indie Game Joe amplified it to a huge audience overnight — a brand-new word entering the gaming vocabulary in a single day. Brushland is coming to Steam (wishlist open, release date unannounced), and this wiki follows it from reveal to release: the mechanics, the world, the comparisons and every release signal in between.

items.question: What is Brushland?
items.answer: A cozy fairytale kingdom-builder from Transhuman Design where you paint the land — mountains, rivers, waterfalls and roads — and the kingdom builds itself: villagers move in automatically and houses change appearance depending on their surroundings. It was revealed October 16, 2026 with an official trailer at The MIX Fall Game Showcase.

items.question: When does Brushland release?
items.answer: No date yet. The Steam page is live with wishlists open and the game is described as coming soon; the release guide tracks every dated signal from the studio and the store page as they appear.

items.question: Who made Brushland?
items.answer: Transhuman Design, a veteran independent studio — the developer Michał introduced the game personally on the Steam page. The studio's catalog spans multiplayer and creative indie titles; Brushland is its cozy storybook turn.

items.question: How does the painting actually work?
items.answer: Terrain is the interface: you brush landforms and water onto the world and the game grows them into full geography — then the villagers take over, settling and adapting houses to whatever you painted. The paint mechanics guide covers every brush the trailer reveals.
